title: Order Collision Risk

statement.md: A market simulation places $n$ agents on a number line; agent $i$ starts at position $x_i$ and moves with constant velocity $v_i$ (positive = rightward). The risk engine must flag whether **any two agents** ever occupy the same position at the same moment during the next $t$ time units.
Positions are distinct at time zero. A collision is a meeting at a strictly positive time $\tau \le t$.

inputFormat: First line: $n$ ($1 \le n \le 2000$). Second line: $n$ integers $x_i$ ($|x_i| \le 10^9$, distinct). Third line: $n$ integers $v_i$ ($|v_i| \le 10^9$). Fourth line: $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^9$).
outputFormat: `COLLIDE` if any pair meets at time $0 < \tau \le t$, otherwise `SAFE`.
constraints: all arithmetic fits in double precision here

examples.explanation: Agents 1 and 2: gap 5 closes at rate 1 → meet at τ=5 ≤ 6.

hints: Relative motion: the gap between i and j changes at rate vi − vj.
Meeting time τ = (xj − xi)/(vi − vj), guard the sign and the zero-divisor before dividing.
Exact boundary: τ = t counts as a collision; τ = 0 does not.

editorial.md: Two agents meet when the initial gap $d_0 = x_j - x_i$ (for $i < j$ in index order, but any consistent orientation works) is closed by the relative speed $dv = v_i - v_j$. If $d_0 \cdot dv > 0$ the gap is closing, and the meeting time is $\tau = d_0 / dv$. Report a collision iff some pair has $0 < \tau \le t$.

The product test $d_0 \cdot dv > 0$ elegantly handles both orderings (faster behind slower, or the mirrored case). $O(n^2)$ at n=2000 is 2M cheap checks, no sorting needed. The sort-based $O(n \log n)$ variant (neighbours in a sorted order can only collide by first becoming adjacent) is a nice extension but unnecessary at these bounds.

solutions.python:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
xs = list(map(int, data[1:1+n]))
vs = list(map(int, data[1+n:1+2*n]))
t = int(data[2*n+1])
collide = False
for i in range(n):
 for j in range(i+1, n):
 d0 = xs[j], xs[i]
 dv = vs[i], vs[j]
 if d0 * dv > 0:
 tau = d0 / dv
 if 0 < tau <= t:
 collide = True
print("COLLIDE" if collide else "SAFE")
